memory_candidates.content: lint-agent-contracts.sh Check K's PROHIBITIVE_MARKER_PATTERN anchor is the literal, case-sensitive set 'MUST NOT|forbidden|prohibited|antipattern', read from bounded-build-waiter.md's Forbidden-Shape Lint Anchor at runtime. When rewording agent-contract prose near a backgrounding phrase (run_in_background) paired with a notification phrase (completion notification) within a ~9-line sliding window, using only 'never'/'NEVER' as the guard word does NOT satisfy the predicate and will trip a real Check K FAIL -- one of the four exact tokens above must appear in the same window. Discovered when Phase 5 of a lean-extension migration discharged Check K's exclusion and the lint immediately found 2 FAILs in prose that had been rewritten using 'never' during an earlier phase.

generate-context-line-counts.sh --write (and deploy-headless.sh's own internal invocation of it before every deploy) regenerates line_count across EVERY extension's index-entries.json in the source store, not only the extension whose file you edited. Editing even one context/pattern/rule file commonly leaves a *different* extension's index-entries.json (e.g. core's, when you only touched core/context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md) silently stale and uncommitted in the working tree after a redeploy, discovered only via a subsequent git status check. When a task's own file_scope doesn't include that index-entries.json path, commit the regenerated line_count fix separately via a direct (no --task) git-commit-scoped.sh call with a 'sync:' message, rather than bundling it into (or silently dropping it from) the phase-commit wrapper.
